plants.name: Camellia japonica
plants.description: Glossy evergreen shrubs covered in rose-like blooms that open in the cool, damp days of winter. The flowers stand out against dark, leathery leaves and can be single, semi-double or fully layered with petals.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring, with peak bloom from about January to March in mild climates
plants.location: Japan, coastal China, and the southeastern United States, such as Georgia and the Carolinas
plants.funFact: Camellia japonica is a close relative of the tea plant, Camellia sinensis. Its seeds are pressed to make camellia oil, which is used in cooking and in traditional Japanese hair care.

plants.name: Prunus mume
plants.description: A small tree that flowers on bare branches while frost is still possible. Its fragrant blossoms appear in clusters and perfume the winter air. Many East Asian gardens plant it to welcome the turning of the year.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-winter to early spring, with peak bloom from late January to March
plants.location: Southern Japan, eastern China, and Korea, in the warmer lowland regions
plants.funFact: In East Asian art and poetry, the plum blossom symbolizes perseverance and hope because it blooms in the cold. It is often paired with pine and bamboo as one of the 'Three Friends of Winter.'

plants.name: Agapanthus praecox
plants.description: Tall, sturdy stems rise from clumps of strappy leaves and carry round clusters of trumpet-shaped flowers. In the Southern Hemisphere summer, the blooms look like blue fireworks along garden borders and roadsides.
plants.bloomingSeason: Southern Hemisphere summer, with flowering from about December to February
plants.location: Native to South Africa's Eastern Cape, and widely grown in Australia and New Zealand
plants.funFact: Despite its common name, the African Lily is not a true lily. The genus name comes from the Greek words for 'love' and 'flower.'
